description:
Programme or Project Overview

The University of Twente invites applications for a PhD position on water footprint assessment and water credit design in Egypt's horticulture sector. The project studies how water use along horticultural value chains can be measured, attributed and incentivised, and designs credit-based instruments that reward water-efficient practice in a water-scarce production landscape.

The candidate will combine water footprint accounting with economic and governance analysis, working across Dutch and Egyptian research partners and with actors in the horticulture sector. Field-level assessments feed into the design and evaluation of water credit mechanisms, connecting hydrological data with finance and policy instruments. The position is a salaried four-year doctoral track under the CAO-NU collective agreement.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in water management, environmental economics, sustainability science or a related discipline, and bring strong quantitative skills and an interest in transdisciplinary fieldwork. Experience with life-cycle or footprint assessment methods and with stakeholder research is an advantage. The working language is English, and the project includes extended collaboration with partners and stakeholders in Egypt.

Highlights

  • Water footprint assessment of horticultural value chains
  • Water credit and incentive instrument design
  • Economic and governance analysis of water use
  • Field assessment with Egyptian sector partners
  • Transdisciplinary sustainability research
  • Salaried four-year PhD under the CAO-NU agreement
